Use this command family to discover, inspect, validate, mutate, render, and trace Entries.

### Command path
`entry` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The shell adapter is `snl entry`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"entry","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. Calling the namespace without a child is valid discovery, not a usage error.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"entry","data":...,"diagnostics":[]}`. `data` contains structured command discovery: child command paths, argument schemas, read/write classification, and one-line summaries.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"entry","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":...,"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Read-only. It must not acquire the writer lock or modify workspace bytes. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. Repeated calls against unchanged bytes return equivalent semantic results.
